claims.text: The starting material is a homogeneous, coarse-grained HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
High-pressure torsion can produce an approximately 50–100 µm nanocrystalline surface layer graded into a coarse-grained core in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed graded surface layer will have high dislocation density and transition gradually into a ductile coarse-grained bulk.
The nanocrystalline surface layer will enhance dislocation storage.
The nanocrystalline surface layer will activate grain-boundary-mediated mechanisms that promote strain hardening.
Enhanced strain hardening in the graded material will delay shear-band development during high-strain-rate adiabatic deformation.
The coarse-grained core will preserve overall ductility and prevent strength gains from causing premature failure.
Robust bonding between the gradient layers is critical for maintaining structural integrity during dynamic loading.
Under adiabatic dynamic compression near 10^3 s^-1, gradient nanostructuring will increase yield strength by approximately 15–25% relative to the stated baseline.
Under adiabatic dynamic compression near 10^3 s^-1, gradient nanostructuring will increase fracture strain or uniform deformation by approximately 20–30% relative to the stated baseline.
The gradual grain-size gradient will delay shear localization under dynamic deformation.
The gradual grain-size gradient will make impact-induced energy release more moderate and gradual.
Variations in gradient-layer thickness, uniformity, and interfacial bonding will affect the magnitude of the dynamic-property improvements.
